Welcome to
Moorcroft School
We are a secondary school for students between 11 and 19 years old with severe learning disabilities (SLD), profound and multiple learning disabilities (PMLD) and autistic spectrum disorders (ASD). Some of the students may also have additional sensory or physical impairments or challenging behaviour.
Moorcroft School pupils attend school at one of two specialist locations. Our main school site in Hillingdon or at the Eden Pinkwell Satellite based at Pinkwell School in Hayes.
At Moorcroft we aim to provide the best possible education outcomes for our students.
All our students have a personalised learning programme to help them achieve their best. We use this to adapt our curriculum to meet their individual needs.
Ellie Hodgkinson, Head of School

Career guidance
Preparing young people with SEND to take the next steps on their career journey.
My skills, my future.
How do we plan individual career support?
We use the 8 ‘Gatsby Benchmarks’ to plan how to best support individual students with career access and decision making.
Community learning
Community learning from KS3 onwards contributes towards preparing students to access their local community and engage in a variety of new experiences and local amenities. This supports students to;
Activities can include:
visits to possible employers in the community
visits to possible future education settings
visits to possible leisure facilities
Work related learning and training
KS4 and 6th form students can take part in a number of tasks around school such as:
preparing the hall for assemblies

Current Affairs
The purpose of learning about current affairs is to understand matters arising locally and nationally such as the latest news on TV, an upcoming festival or celebration, life events of students or an interesting social story. This subject aims at Social, Moral, Spiritual and Cultural development and at developing students’ citizenship skills. It provides our students with a breadth of knowledge about the wider world as well as ensuring a weekly element of novelty in the curriculum.
Food Technology
Food Technology is taught in our specialist cooking room and in classrooms to make it accessible for all. This subject allows our students to practice their Maths, English and life skills in a functional context.
Health and Fitness
Our students not only develop gross and fine motor skills, but they also learn about a healthy and moderate lifestyle as well as healthy nutrition.
Our students regularly visit their local community. They also attend swimming sessions in community pools.

Key Stage 4 Overview
Key Stage 5 – 6th Form
The sixth form curriculum focuses on enhancing students functional and practical skills needed for independence in adulthood. The future destination helps create a bespoke timetable which include lessons such as Enterprise, Home management, Cooking, Health and fitness and work experience/training. There is a strong emphasise on students living in the real world therefore most of their lessons and learning takes place off site and within the community.
The students follow an individualised curriculum that reflects their skills, abilities, needs and interests. We ensure all activities build upon prior knowledge and skills. Learners are taught how to generalise their skills and complete them with greater fluency and independence.
All sixth form students complete a number of accredited courses such as AQA, ASDAN and Equals. The accredited modules have a strong focus on functional skills for life.

Key Stage 5 Overview
Sensory Curriculum
We use a wide range of activities, such as Intensive Interaction, sensory exploration, sensory stories, cause and effect activities and adapted technology provision. Our curriculum strands focus on the development of expressive and receptive skills, problem solving and exploration, skills for learning and life and body control.
Our main goal is to empower our students and develop their self-advocacy skills. We want them to actively communicate their needs and make choices and decisions about themselves as well as learn how to exert control over their environment through a range of highly personalised activities; they are active participants in their learning and their daily routines.
We place a large emphasis on the process of lifelong learning, as we want our students to enjoy the opportunities in life to the fullest, make friends and experience success.
What is more, we always acknowledge that our students are young adults and we reflect this in age-appropriate and highly stimulating activities. We want the personalities of our students to shine through and we respect their individual preferences.
Our students have also opportunities to integrate within both the school and the wider community. This takes place through educational visits, weekly departmental assemblies, cross-school curriculum events and performances.

Admissions
Friends of Moorcroft
The Friends of Moorcroft, or FROMS as it is more affectionately known, is a registered charity established to raise funds for Moorcroft School.
The FROMS committee comprises of parents and staff who meet regularly to look at ways of generating more money to support our students and to organise a series of social events throughout the school year.
We have raised money to help install a new dark room and a sensory garden.
If you are looking for a place for a child or a young person, please contact the school office to arrange a visit. You will be given a tour of the school by a senior member of staff and will have an opportunity to meet students and staff and ask lots of questions.
We encourage parents or carers to bring their child with them so we can start to assess whether the school will be suitable for them. We can also visit you and your child at home if you prefer.
If you decide you wish to apply for a place then you will need to contact the SEND team in your Local Authority.
New admissions to our School either will have an Education Health Care Plan or be undergoing the statutory process towards such.
Your Local Authority will consult with the school and if we are able to offer your child a place, they will decide whether to name Moorcroft in the Education Health and Care Plan, or in the statement.

Wearing uniform is encouraged because we know that putting on a school uniform is an important part of daily routines for many of our pupils. However, we do understand that some pupils find wearing school uniform difficult so it is optional.
